BIDV SUSTAINABILITY REPORT 2025
Report Profile
The 2025 Sustainability Report of the Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam 
(BIDV) has been prepared to provide transparent, comprehensive, and structured information on the Bank’s strategy, 
activities, and performance in achieving its sustainable development objectives during the 2025 financial year.
The Report has been approved by the Board of Directors of BIDV under Decision No. 376/QĐ-BIDV and reflects the 
Bank’s integration of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors into its governance and management 
practices.
PURPOSE OF THE REPORT
BASIS OF PREPARATION
The Report has been prepared in accordance with the principles of accuracy, objectivity, consistency, and 
comparability across reporting periods, while progressively aligning with international best practices and 
ESG assessment requirements in the capital markets.
REPORTING PRINCIPLES
The Report presents official information on BIDV’s strategies, policies, initiatives, and performance across 
Environmental (E), Social (S), and Governance (G) aspects for the financial year from January 1, 2025 to 
December 31, 2025.
•	 Reporting frequency:  Annual.
•	 Reporting data:  The Report covers BIDV’s operations, including its Head Office, 175 branches, and 
927 transaction offices across 34 provinces and cities in Vietnam.  
Financial data disclosed in the Report are referenced from the Bank’s audited consolidated financial 
statements for 2025. 
REPORTING SCOPE
BIDV welcomes all feedback and comments regarding the content of this Sustainability Report via the

Message from the
Chairman of the Board of Directors
Mr. Phan Duc Tu
Chairman of the Board of Directors
Dear Shareholders, Valued Customers, Partners, 
Employees, and Stakeholders,
On behalf of the Board of Directors of the Joint Stock 
Commercial Bank for Investment and Development 
of Vietnam (BIDV), I would like to express my sincere 
appreciation for your continued trust and support 
over the years.
Sustainability Strategy
In the context where sustainable development and 
green transition have become inevitable global 
trends, BIDV identifies these as core orientations 
embedded throughout its development strategy. 
As early as the 2021–2025 period, the Bank has 
proactively integrated ESG as a fundamental 
component of its long-term strategy, with “Green” 
positioned as a central pillar, aiming to become a 
leading bank in sustainable development in Vietnam. 
BIDV’s sustainability strategy is implemented in a 
comprehensive and integrated manner across three 
pillars – Environmental, Social, and Governance – 
supported by a system of clearly defined targets, 
quantitative indicators, and transparent monitoring 
mechanisms, aligned with international standards 
and best practices.
Leading Bank in Green and Sustainable Finance  
BIDV continues to affirm its pioneering role in green 
finance, maintaining a leading position in both scale 
and growth rate in the market. As of the end of 2025, 
the Bank’s outstanding green credit reached VND 
82,332 billion, achieving an impressive compound 
annual growth rate (CAGR) of 20.8% during the 
2021–2025 period. The portfolio focuses on key 
sectors such as renewable energy, sustainable 
infrastructure, green agriculture, and the circular 
economy. The Bank has also implemented a wide 
range of large-scale green financing programs for 
both corporate and retail customers, contributing 
to the promotion of sustainable lifestyles and 
production models within the community.
In parallel, BIDV has taken the lead in developing 
the green capital market through its Green and 
Sustainable Bond Framework, which has been rated 
SQS2 (“Very Good”) by Moody’s. The Bank has 
cumulatively issued VND 8,350 billion in bonds for 
eligible projects. In 2025, BIDV further strengthened 
its sustainable finance ecosystem by updating its 
Sustainable Loan Framework (Version 2.0), aligned 
with the Green Taxonomy under Decision No. 
21/2025/QĐ-TTg of the Government; launching its 
Sustainable Deposit Framework with mobilized 
funds reaching nearly VND 7,000 billion; and 
expanding sustainability-linked loans (SLLs) tied to 
specific ESG targets. These initiatives contribute to 
enhancing asset quality while supporting clients in 
fulfilling their sustainability commitments.
Pioneering Comprehensive Digital Transformation
BIDV continues to accelerate its comprehensive 
digital transformation to build a green banking 
ecosystem. Digital platforms such as SmartBanking, 
BIDV Direct, along with ecosystems including 
TradeFlat, SCF, and OpenAPI,... enhance customer 
experience and promote cashless transactions. By 
2025, the proportion of products and services fully 
delivered through digital channels reached 78% 
for retail customers and 69% for corporate clients. 
Internally, digitalization initiatives have contributed 
to optimizing operations, reducing paper usage, 
and improving governance efficiency, with the 
digitization rate of internal workflows across the 
system reaching an impressive 85%.
Advancing a transparent governance system with 
integrated ESG factors in line with international 
standards
On the governance front, BIDV remains committed 
to building a transparent corporate governance 
model that complies with applicable regulations 
and aligns with international best practices. ESG 
factors are systematically integrated into the Bank’s 
risk management framework, with 100% of credit 
projects subject to environmental risk assessment 
under standardized procedures, while the Bank 
continues to enhance its climate risk management 
framework and develop a modern ESG data 
system to support measurement, monitoring, and 
disclosure.
Proud to be a bank that promotes human values and 
accompanies the community’s development
As a socially responsible bank, BIDV continues to 
foster human-centric values through social welfare 
programs with total funding exceeding VND 500 
billion in 2025, focusing on education, healthcare, 
housing, and disaster relief, while also implementing 
environmental initiatives such as the “One Million 
Trees” Program, community flood-resilient housing, 
and the “Clean Water for a Green Life” initiative,... The 
Bank also advances financial inclusion by improving 
access to capital for businesses, particularly SMEs, 
aligned with ESG criteria to enhance credit quality 
and guide sustainable capital flows.
Grounded in a strong commitment to the rule of 
law, BIDV fully fulfills its obligations to the State and 
maintains transparency in information disclosure, 
thereby strengthening stakeholder trust and laying 
a solid foundation for long-term development. In 
2025, BIDV contributed nearly VND 13,000 billion to 
the State budget, maintaining its position as one of 
the leading corporate taxpayers in Vietnam.
Developing human capital, enhancing customer 
experience, and safeguarding data security
BIDV is committed to building a “Happy Workplace” 
through 
a 
positive 
working 
environment, 
comprehensive employee benefits, and continuous 
training and development. In terms of customer 
experience, the Bank continues to deliver superior 
service quality while continuously enhancing its 
products and services, achieving a Customer 
Satisfaction Score (CSAT) of nearly 97% and a 
Net Promoter Score (NPS) of nearly 80% in 2025. 
Data protection and information security are 
consistently 
strengthened 
through 
advanced 
security systems, ensuring safe operations and 
regulatory compliance.
Affirming 
credibility 
and 
integration 
capacity 
through international partnerships
BIDV 
continues 
to 
strengthen 
international 
cooperation in sustainable finance by expanding 
partnerships with leading financial institutions and 
banks such as the World Bank, IFC, ADB, HSBC, 
MUFG, and Hana Bank, among others, to support 
energy transition and emissions reduction projects 
in Vietnam. A significant milestone was achieved 
on October 28, 2025, when BIDV became the first 
commercial bank in Vietnam to be accredited as 
an Accredited Entity of the Green Climate Fund 
(GCF). This recognition not only affirms BIDV’s 
governance capacity and international credibility, 
but also opens up new opportunities for the Bank 
to further lead the development of Vietnam’s 
green finance market. This milestone represents an 
important step forward, contributing to the deeper 
integration of Vietnam’s banking system into the 
global sustainable finance landscape.
With the solid foundation established and the 
continued support of our stakeholders, BIDV is 
confident in its ability to achieve further milestones 
in its sustainable development journey, contributing 
meaningfully to the prosperity of the nation.
Once again, on behalf of the Board of Directors of 
BIDV, I would like to express my sincere appreciation 
to 
our 
shareholders, 
customers, 
partners, 
employees, and all stakeholders for their continued 
trust and support.
Sincerely,
CHAIRMAN OF THE
BOARD OF DIRECTORS
Phan Duc Tu

bank’s core strategic pillars. Accordingly, the Bank has defined major initiatives and 
specific targets for green banking development, including maintaining green credit 
growth at 20–25% (higher than the overall system credit growth rate) and achieving 
reductions in operational emissions.

ESG GOVERNANCE MODEL
The year 2026 marks a significant milestone in BIDV’s ESG governance with the establishment of the 
Sustainability Committee under the Board of Directors and the Sustainability Council under the Chief 
Executive Officer; notably, the Bank has, for the first time, designated a member of the Executive Board 
Member in charge of Sustainability (Chief Sustainability Officer – CSO), assigned to Deputy Chief Executive 
Officer Tran Phuong.
The strengthening of ESG governance structures at all levels reflects BIDV’s strong commitment to 
implementing its Sustainability Strategy and ESG practices across the entire system, in pursuit of its strategic 
vision of becoming a “Large – Strong – Green” bank in the coming period.
BIDV fully recognizes the critical role of integrating Environmental, Social, and Governance 
(ESG) factors into its business operations to ensure sustainable development and create 
long-term value for stakeholders. In response to increasing sustainability requirements, the 
Bank continuously enhances its ESG governance model in a comprehensive, effective, and 
internationally aligned manner.

Periodic monitoring and evaluation of governance practices  
BIDV’s governance capacity is continuously measured and enhanced through a structured evaluation mechanism: 
•	 Regular assessment under ACGS: Conducted semi-annually (on June 30 and December 31), with the 
Secretariat & Investor Relations Division acting as the focal point in coordination to assess corporate 
governance practices against ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard criteria.
•	 Continuous improvement: Evaluation results are submitted to senior management for approval and 
disclosed in the Annual Report. For areas not aligned with international best practices, the focal unit 
proposes improvement actions and assigns responsibilities for subsequent implementation cycles.
•	 Strategic oversight: The Board of Directors is responsible for setting direction and comprehensively 
overseeing the implementation of the ESG strategy, ensuring sustainable development goals are deeply 
integrated into business plans and the Bank’s competitive positioning.
Transparent appointment and remuneration policies 
Appointment process: BIDV applies the highest standards in appointing members of the Board of Directors 
and the Supervisory Board. Information on candidates (upon approval by the State Bank of Vietnam) is 
disclosed on the Bank’s website in accordance with regulations, ensuring shareholders have sufficient time 
to review and make informed decisions.
Candidate criteria: Leadership candidates must meet stringent requirements in terms of professional 
qualifications (Bachelor’s degree or higher), banking management experience, and, importantly, professional 
ethics standards as prescribed by the Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam.
Remuneration policy: 
•	 Remuneration and compensation for the Board of Directors, Supervisory Board, and Executive Board 
are provided fairly, linked to performance outcomes, and within the budget approved by the General 
Meeting of Shareholders, ensuring both motivation and long-term alignment.
•	 Detailed information on remuneration and compensation for the Board of Directors, Supervisory Board, 
and Executive Board is fully disclosed in BIDV’s financial statements and annual reports.
Protection of creditors’ rights
As part of strengthening its governance framework and aligning with international best practices, BIDV has 
issued specific guidelines on the Policy for Protection of Creditors’ Rights. This policy affirms creditors as 
key stakeholders and strategic partners in the Bank’s sustainable development.
The core contents of the policy include
Based on the Law on Recovery and Bankruptcy 2025 and relevant legal regulations, BIDV defines its creditors 
to include, but not be limited to, the following:
•	 Organizations and individuals depositing funds at BIDV.
•	 Holders of certain debt instruments issued by BIDV, such as bonds, bills of exchange, certificates of 
deposit, promissory notes, etc.
•	 Organizations and individuals providing credit to BIDV in forms such as loans or guarantees.
•	 Beneficiaries (guaranteed parties) under valid guarantee letters issued by BIDV.
•	 Lessors of assets, premises, or facilities used by BIDV for its operations.
•	 Organizations and individuals supplying goods and services to BIDV.

•	 Other entities having creditor rights toward BIDV in accordance with applicable laws.
The classification of secured, unsecured, and partially secured creditors depends on contractual terms and 
agreements between the creditor and BIDV regarding collateral arrangements (if any), in compliance with 
relevant legal provisions.
Commitment to safeguarding core creditor rights:
The Bank implements strict oversight mechanisms to ensure creditors fully exercise the following rights:
•	 Right to payment: nsuring full and timely settlement of committed financial obligations.
•	 ight to access information: Providing timely and accurate disclosures on financial conditions to enable 
creditors to exercise their rights.
•	 Collateral rights: For secured creditors, BIDV respects the right to enforce collateral in accordance with 
contractual agreements.
•	 Legal and judicial rights: Creditors are entitled to claim damages, impose penalties, initiate legal 
proceedings at courts/arbitration, or file for bankruptcy/recovery procedures in accordance with the Law 
on Recovery and Bankruptcy 2025.
BIDV’s governance and oversight responsibilities:
To ensure effective implementation, the Bank assigns clear responsibilities to relevant units to:
•	 Manage liquidity: Maintain funding balance to ensure continuous payment capacity to creditors.
•	 Ensure accurate accounting: Record all liabilities, interest, and payable fees fully and accurately.
•	 Control systemic risks: Regularly monitor and assess credit, liquidity, and market risks that may directly 
affect repayment capacity.
•	 Provide effective resolution mechanisms: Promptly address complaints and disputes, while proactively 
identifying and mitigating actions that may harm creditors’ interests.
The formalization of creditor protection policies in line with the latest legal standards not only 
reinforces BIDV’s integrity in business conduct but also serves as a foundation to strengthen 
its credit ratings, thereby maintaining its position as a trusted partner of international 
financial institutions.
